# Society Social x Sunbrella Interiors Debuts Performance Fabric Collection

[**Lindsay Brown**](https://www.wf-vision.com/profile/lbrown/)// September 21, 2026

- [![twitter](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/x-logo+black.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Society+Social+x+Sunbrella+Interiors+Debuts+Performance+Fabric+Collection&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Ffabric-collection%2Fsociety-social-x-sunbrella-interiors-debuts-performance-fabric-collection%2F)
- [![facebook](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/facebook.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Ffabric-collection%2Fsociety-social-x-sunbrella-interiors-debuts-performance-fabric-collection%2F)
- [![linkedin](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/linkedin.svg)](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Ffabric-collection%2Fsociety-social-x-sunbrella-interiors-debuts-performance-fabric-collection%2F&title=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Ffabric-collection%2Fsociety-social-x-sunbrella-interiors-debuts-performance-fabric-collection%2F)
- [![pinterest](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/pinterest.svg)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Ffabric-collection%2Fsociety-social-x-sunbrella-interiors-debuts-performance-fabric-collection%2F&media=&description=)
- [![email](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/email.svg)](mailto:?subject=Society%20Social%20x%20Sunbrella%20Interiors%20Debuts%20Performance%20Fabric%20Collection&body= "Share by Email")

Performance fabric is getting a colorful update. [Society Social](https://www.shopsocietysocial.com/) has teamed up with [Sunbrella Interiors](https://www.sunbrella.com/indoor-living?srsltid=AU7gw4WjIqNmkn32rDVVvLsJWFos8YbNZC5giKoogDdlcVjRey1p3z-o) on a new collection that brings the lifestyle brand’s playful, pattern-forward aesthetic to durable textiles designed for everyday living.

[![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Photo-Aug-04-2026-10-34-53-AM-200x300.jpg)](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Photo-Aug-04-2026-10-34-53-AM-scaled.jpg) The [Society Social](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/society-social/ "Posts tagged with Society Social") x [Sunbrella](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/sunbrella/ "Posts tagged with Sunbrella") Interiors collection includes more than 25 exclusive stain- and liquid-resistant fabrics, ranging from lively patterns and classic stripes to versatile solids. Standouts include Veranda Vine, a fresh botanical motif, and Performance Pinstripe, a tailored take on a timeless stripe.

Founded by Roxy Owens in 2011, Society Social has built its identity around a spirited approach to traditional design, favoring color, pattern and personality over pared-back neutrals. The new collaboration translates that signature look into [performance fabrics](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/performance-fabrics/ "Posts tagged with performance fabrics") made to handle the realities of busy homes.

The collection is available by the yard and across several of Society Social’s best-selling furniture designs, including the Aurora Roll Arm Tight Back Ruffle Sofa, Hudson Wingback Chair and Hadley Wavy Bench.

With its mix of practical performance and unapologetically pretty design, the collection makes a case for furniture that doesn’t have to choose between looking good and living well.

# New & Noteworthy Finds for September

[**Lindsay Brown**](https://www.wf-vision.com/profile/lbrown/)// September 21, 2026

- [![twitter](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/x-logo+black.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=New+%26+Noteworthy+Finds+for+September&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdesign-and-trends%2Fnew-noteworthy-finds-for-september%2F)
- [![facebook](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/facebook.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdesign-and-trends%2Fnew-noteworthy-finds-for-september%2F)
- [![linkedin](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/linkedin.svg)](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdesign-and-trends%2Fnew-noteworthy-finds-for-september%2F&title=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdesign-and-trends%2Fnew-noteworthy-finds-for-september%2F)
- [![pinterest](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/pinterest.svg)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdesign-and-trends%2Fnew-noteworthy-finds-for-september%2F&media=&description=)
- [![email](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/email.svg)](mailto:?subject=New%20&%20Noteworthy%20Finds%20for%20September&body= "Share by Email")

This month’s latest launches pair smart innovation with plenty of style. Clever motorization, fresh textiles, unexpected collaborations and handcrafted design are giving us plenty to talk about, along with a few industry developments worth watching.

**[![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Lee-Jofa-weezie-300x300.jpg)](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Lee-Jofa-weezie.jpg) Bathing Beauty**

Heritage textile house Lee Jofa brings some of its most recognizable patterns to the bath in a new collaboration with luxury linens brand Weezie. Designed as a coordinated “wardrobe” for the bathroom, the collection spans plush towels and robes, shower curtains and accessories, reimagining archival florals, stripes and botanicals for everyday use. Signature Lee Jofa patterns, including Palermo and Davenport, mingle with Marciana, an exclusive design created for the collaboration, while Weezie’s piped edges and customizable monograms add a personalized finishing touch. [**WeezieTowels.com**](http://weezietowels.com/)

**[![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Carsan_DualMotion-Blinds-300x169.jpg)](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Carsan_DualMotion-Blinds-scaled.jpg) Smooth Operator**

DualMotion by [Carsan](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/carsan/ "Posts tagged with carsan") Window Fashions goes beyond traditional motorized horizontal blinds. Where other motorized faux wood systems tilt only, DualMotion delivers both lift and tilt from a single integrated motor, giving full control of light, privacy and view-through. Paired with Carsan’s ScrolControl remote, a precision scroll wheel dials in exact slat position. The engineering earned Carsan the 2025 WCMA Best New Technical Innovation Award for Horizontal Blinds (All Finishes) and Motorization and Automation. Built by a 50-year vertically integrated manufacturer selling exclusively to the trade, DualMotion gives dealers one clean, cordless motorized solution to specify and sell. [**CarsanWF.com**](http://carsanwf.com/)

**[![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Coulisse-300x200.jpg)](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Coulisse.jpg) On a Roll**

[Coulisse](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/coulisse/ "Posts tagged with coulisse") refreshes a staple with its new Roller Collection, bringing together an expanded assortment of performance-driven and design-forward fabrics. Organized across five dedicated books, the collection includes Light Filtering, Black-out, Nature, Screen Textile and Screen Function options. New recycled and nature-inspired textiles join proven bestsellers, offering designers and dealers a broad range of colors, textures and performance features, all in stock and ready to ship. [**Coulisse.com**](http://coulisse.com/)

**[![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/FermWicker-300x300.jpg)](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/FermWicker.jpg) Wicker Dreams**

While we may never get a wicker husband who looks like Alexander Skarsgård, we can weave a little cottagecore into our homes with ferm LIVING’s Dou Floor Lamp ahead of _Wicker_‘s October 23 release. Meticulously hand-braided from natural rattan, the sculptural lamp features a conical shade supported by a durable iron frame. Its open weave casts a warm glow while adding texture and organic appeal, with subtle variations in color and shape making each handcrafted piece one of a kind. [**FermLiving.com**](http://fermliving.com/)

**[![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Somfy-short-copy-300x142.jpg)](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Somfy-short-copy.jpg) Small but Mighty**

Somfy is expanding motorization possibilities with the Roll Up 30 Short, a compact motor designed for narrow windows that may have previously required manual shades. Approximately 3 inches shorter than the standard Roll Up 30, it delivers 2Nm of lifting capacity while helping maximize visible glass. Compatible with existing Sonesse accessories and available with Power over Ethernet or Somfy Digital Network, the motor gives dealers and designers greater flexibility to bring automated shading to smaller openings while maintaining a consistent look across a project. [**SomfySystems.com**](http://somfysystems.com/)

**[![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/1.-Inpros-new-Mint-Hill-Facility-3-300x200.jpg)](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/1.-Inpros-new-Mint-Hill-Facility-3.jpg) Room to Grow**

Inpro is expanding its U.S. manufacturing footprint with a new 165,000-square-foot facility in Mint Hill, North Carolina, bringing two previously separate operations under one roof and adding capacity to support its growing customer base. The company is also investing in its Muskego, Wisconsin, headquarters, where it recently opened a new Design Center + Showroom and plans to open a 30,000-square-foot manufacturing facility later this year. Together, the expansions strengthen Inpro’s manufacturing capabilities and support continued growth across its portfolio of commercial architectural products, including window treatments. [**InproCorp.com**](http://inprocorp.com/)

# TWOPAGES Names Winners of 2026 ‘Curtain as Art’ Design Contest

Three winning curtain collections are now available for purchase following a global competition that drew 825 designers from 56 countries.

[**Lindsay Brown**](https://www.wf-vision.com/profile/lbrown/)// September 21, 2026

- [![twitter](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/x-logo+black.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=TWOPAGES+Names+Winners+of+2026+%E2%80%98Curtain+as+Art%E2%80%99+Design+Contest&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdesign-and-trends%2Ftwopages-names-winners-of-2026-curtain-as-art-design-contest%2F)
- [![facebook](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/facebook.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdesign-and-trends%2Ftwopages-names-winners-of-2026-curtain-as-art-design-contest%2F)
- [![linkedin](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/linkedin.svg)](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdesign-and-trends%2Ftwopages-names-winners-of-2026-curtain-as-art-design-contest%2F&title=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdesign-and-trends%2Ftwopages-names-winners-of-2026-curtain-as-art-design-contest%2F)
- [![pinterest](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/pinterest.svg)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdesign-and-trends%2Ftwopages-names-winners-of-2026-curtain-as-art-design-contest%2F&media=&description=)
- [![email](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/email.svg)](mailto:?subject=TWOPAGES%20Names%20Winners%20of%202026%20%E2%80%98Curtain%20as%20Art%E2%80%99%20Design%20Contest&body= "Share by Email")

[TWOPAGES](https://twopagescurtains.com/) announced the winners of its 2026 [TWOPAGES](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/twopages/ "Posts tagged with TWOPAGES") X [Design Contest](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/design-contest/ "Posts tagged with Design Contest"), themed “Curtain as Art,” during a finale in [New York](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/new-york/ "Posts tagged with New York") on Sept. 16, awarding top honors to British designer Heather Cantrill for her collection, “The Cotswold Way.”

[![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/20260921012831EDT_image_1-1024x576.jpg)](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/20260921012831EDT_image_1-scaled.jpg)

Cantrill received the $10,000 first-place prize, followed by American designer Hailey Kiefer, who earned second place and $8,000 for “Villa Chinoiserie.” Canadian designer Gabrielle De Winter took third place and a $6,000 prize for “Heirloom Studies.”

All three winning collections launched on the TWOPAGES website the same day, turning the designers’ concepts into commercially available curtain collections.

Now in its second year, the contest attracted 1,082 entries from 825 designers representing 56 countries. The competition was created to bring original textile and pattern designs from concept through product development and ultimately into consumers’ homes. All six winning collections from the inaugural 2025 competition also remain available through TWOPAGES.

During the New York finale, finalists presented their collections through videos and live presentations. Building on the “Curtain as Art” theme, the event featured large-scale fabric installations inspired by the three collections, along with dance performances based on the designs.

[![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/20260921012831EDT_image_3-1024x683.jpg)](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/20260921012831EDT_image_3-scaled.jpg) TWOPAGES CEO Ray Chen with the 2026 Contest Jury

The 2026 jury included interior designer Jennifer Farrell; Leatrice Eiseman, executive director of the [Pantone](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/pantone/ "Posts tagged with Pantone") Color Institute; Ingrid Abramovitch; and Bari J. Ackerman. The judges evaluated the finalists following their presentations and discussions.

The event also marked the third anniversary of TWOPAGES’ collaboration with interior designer and content creator Sara Le.

“We want designers’ ideas to be seen and, more importantly, to become part of everyday life,” said Ray Chen, founder and CEO of TWOPAGES. “Through this competition, we bring different cultures and personal stories into curtain design and work with designers to turn their ideas into something that can truly belong in people’s homes.”

The [Heather Cantrill x TWOPAGES,](https://twopagescurtains.com/collections/heather-cantrill-x-twopages) [Hailey Kiefer x TWOPAGES](https://twopagescurtains.com/collections/hailey-kiefer-x-twopages) and [Gabrielle De Winter x TWOPAGES](https://twopagescurtains.com/collections/gabrielle-de-winter-x-twopages) collections are available now at [twopagescurtains.com.](https://twopagescurtains.com/)

# Nominate Your Favorite Brands for VISION’s Second Annual 2026 Readers’ Choice Awards!

Window covering professionals are invited to recognize the brands, products and partners they know, trust and love

[**Lindsay Brown**](https://www.wf-vision.com/profile/lbrown/)// September 16, 2026

- [![twitter](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/x-logo+black.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Nominate+Your+Favorite+Brands+for+VISION%E2%80%99s+Second+Annual+2026+Readers%E2%80%99+Choice+Awards%21&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fnominate-your-favorite-brands-for-visions-second-annual-2026-readers-choice-awards%2F)

Nominations are officially open for [Window Fashion VISION’s Second Annual 2026 Readers’ Choice Awards](http://wf-vision.com/readers-choice-awards-2026/), giving professionals across the window covering industry the opportunity to recognize their favorite brands, products and industry partners. Following an incredible inaugural year with more than 21,000 votes cast, the awards return with 43 categories celebrating excellence across fabrication, motorization, textiles, outdoor products, technology, hardware, retail and more.

Dealers, designers, workrooms, installers, retailers, manufacturers and other industry professionals are encouraged to nominate the companies they know, trust and value. Whether it is a go-to fabric supplier, a trusted fabrication partner, an innovative motorization brand or a company delivering outstanding service, the Readers’ Choice Awards put industry recognition directly in the hands of the professionals who work with these brands every day.

“The Readers’ Choice Awards give our industry a direct voice in recognizing the brands, products and partners that make a meaningful difference in their businesses,” said Lindsay Brown, Managing Editor. “After the tremendous response to our inaugural awards, we are excited to once again invite professionals across the industry to celebrate the companies and innovators they believe are setting the standard.”

**[Nominate](https://www.wf-vision.com/readers-choice-awards-2026/) your favorite brands now through October 15, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time. The nominees receiving the strongest industry support will advance to the official voting round, beginning October 19, 2026, at 1:00 a.m. Eastern Time.**

**2026 Readers’ Choice Award Categories**

**Components**

- Best Hardware Supplier
- Best Motor Manufacturer

**Fabrication**

- Best Custom Workroom
- Best Shade Fabrication
- Best Workroom Partner for Designers

**Motorization**

- Best Control Systems/Smart Home Integration
- Best Integrated Smart Solution
- Best Motor Manufacturer
- Best Motorized Drapery Hardware
- Best Motorized Solution
- Best Retractable Awning
- Power & Battery Innovation

**Hardware & Trimmings**

- Best Decorative Hardware
- Best Decorative Trimming
- Best Motorized Drapery Hardware

**Textiles**

- Best Decorative Fabrics
- Best Exterior Shade & Screen Fabric
- Best in Sustainability
- Best Interior Shade Fabric
- Best [Performance Fabrics](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/performance-fabrics/ "Posts tagged with performance fabrics")

**Outdoor**

- Best Decorative Fabric
- Best Decorative Hardware
- Best Exterior Shade/Screen
- Best Outdoor Living Innovation
- Best Retractable Awning

**Commercial**

- Best Exterior Solution
- Best Interior Solution

**Franchise & Retail**

- Best Franchise
- Best Retail/Showroom Experience

**Groups & Associations**

- Best Buying Group & Association

**Machinery & Equipment**

- Best Machinery Supplier
- Best Workroom Supplies & Tools

**Niche & Noteworthy**

- Best Child Safety Innovation
- Best Dealer Experience
- Best Designer Collaboration
- Best Social Impact & Community
- Best Trade Program
- Industry-Leading Innovator

**PR, Marketing & Consulting**

- Best Consulting & Education
- Best Marketing & Social Media

**Technology**

- Best Design Visualization Tools
- Best Measuring/Quoting Software
- Power & Battery Innovation

Industry professionals may submit nominations in as many applicable categories as they choose. Once voting opens, the window covering community will have the opportunity to support the finalists and determine who earns the title of a 2026 [Window Fashion VISION](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/window-fashion-vision/ "Posts tagged with Window Fashion VISION") Readers’ Choice Award winner.

Nominate the brands you love now by visiting [wf-vision.com/readers-choice-awards-2026/](https://www.wf-vision.com/readers-choice-awards-2026/).

**About Window Fashion VISION**

Window Fashion VISION is the leading publication serving the window covering industry, delivering business insights, design inspiration, product innovation and [industry news](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/industry-news/ "Posts tagged with Industry News") to designers, dealers, retailers, fabricators, workrooms, installers, manufacturers and other professionals. Through its print and digital platforms, educational initiatives and industry programs, VISION connects and celebrates the people and companies shaping the future of window coverings.

- [![email](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/email.svg)](mailto:?subject=Sherwin-Williams%20Names%20Celery%20Its%202027%20Color%20of%20the%20Year&body= "Share by Email")

Green is staying in the spotlight for 2027. [Sherwin-Williams](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/sherwin-williams/ "Posts tagged with Sherwin-Williams") and HGTV Home by Sherwin-Williams have named **[Celery](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/celery/ "Posts tagged with Celery")** their shared 2027 Color of the Year.

A soft, muted green with subtle yellow undertones, Celery SW 6421 brings a fresh, airy feel to [interiors](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/interiors/ "Posts tagged with interiors") while tapping into the continued pull toward [nature-inspired color](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/nature-inspired-color/ "Posts tagged with nature-inspired color") and restorative spaces.

Part of Sherwin-Williams’ 2027 [Colormix Trend Forecast](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/colormix-trend-forecast/ "Posts tagged with colormix trend forecast"), [Rewild](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/rewild/ "Posts tagged with Rewild"), Celery is designed to feel both calming and uplifting. Its versatility allows it to move easily from contemporary and transitional spaces to heritage-inspired and nature-driven interiors.

“Celery was chosen as the 2027 Color of the Year because it reflects today’s priorities: [wellness](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/wellness/ "Posts tagged with wellness"), [balance](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/balance/ "Posts tagged with balance") and connection,” said Ashley Banbury, color marketing manager at Sherwin-Williams.

The shade can be paired with soft neutrals and earthy greens or pushed in a bolder direction with colors including Kirsch Red, Plum Brown, Potentially Purple and Georgian Bay.

Celery SW 6421 is available through Sherwin-Williams and as Celery HGSW6421 through HGTV Home by Sherwin-Williams.

# disCOVER the Sep/Oct issue of Window Fashion VISION

[**Lindsay Brown**](https://www.wf-vision.com/profile/lbrown/)// September 14, 2026

- [![twitter](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/x-logo+black.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=disCOVER+the+Sep%2FOct+issue+of+Window+Fashion+VISION&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdiscover%2Fdiscover-the-sep-oct-issue-of-window-fashion-vision%2F)
- [![facebook](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/facebook.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdiscover%2Fdiscover-the-sep-oct-issue-of-window-fashion-vision%2F)
- [![linkedin](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/linkedin.svg)](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdiscover%2Fdiscover-the-sep-oct-issue-of-window-fashion-vision%2F&title=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdiscover%2Fdiscover-the-sep-oct-issue-of-window-fashion-vision%2F)
- [![pinterest](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/pinterest.svg)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fdiscover%2Fdiscover-the-sep-oct-issue-of-window-fashion-vision%2F&media=&description=)
- [![email](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/email.svg)](mailto:?subject=disCOVER%20the%20Sep/Oct%20issue%20of%20Window%20Fashion%20VISION&body= "Share by Email")

With water views from every window, this [Marco Island](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/marco-island/ "Posts tagged with Marco Island"), [Florida](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/florida/ "Posts tagged with Florida"), primary bedroom offered designer Sandra Asdourian plenty of inspiration for its dreamy blue palette.

Part of a new-build home designed by [Sandra Asdourian Interiors](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/sandra-asdourian-interiors/ "Posts tagged with Sandra Asdourian Interiors"), the bedroom was created as a quiet, calming retreat where the homeowner could unwind and sleep peacefully. Asdourian embraced the home’s coastal surroundings, color-drenching the ceiling, trim and walls in [Sherwin-Williams](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/sherwin-williams/ "Posts tagged with Sherwin-Williams")‘ Smoky Azurite.

[![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Pages-from-WFV_SO_Web-231x300.jpg)](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Pages-from-WFV_SO_Web.jpg)

**View the Sep/Oct issue [here](https://issuu.com/wfvision/docs/wfv_so_digital_issue_2026)!**

A hand-knotted rug in shades of blue, green and teal helped set the palette for the rest of the room. At the windows, Asdourian selected [Kravet](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/kravet/ "Posts tagged with Kravet")‘s Lost Coast fabric for the [custom drapery](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/custom-drapery/ "Posts tagged with custom drapery") and [roman shades](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/roman-shades/ "Posts tagged with Roman shades"). “I sourced a fabric that felt like the waves on the beach and built the colors and textures around those elements,” Asdourian said.

[![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/2-200x300.jpg)](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/2-scaled.jpg) Photography by Tristin Heeb

Even with color covering nearly every surface, the room never feels overwhelming. Asdourian balanced the saturated blues with soothing wood tones and other quieter elements. “When I go bold with color, I also add places for the eye to rest.”

The window treatments add another layer of color while providing the light control essential to a restful bedroom. The drapery and roman shades are fully lined, and [motorized blackout shades](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/motorized-blackout-shades/ "Posts tagged with motorized blackout shades") at every window make it easy to darken the room when needed.

Satin brass hardware adds warmth to the window treatments, while Peacock Alley’s Biagio Jacquard bedding and Visual Comfort lamps in a glazed Blue Lagoon finish carry the palette throughout the space. Custom pillows and a one-of-a-kind rug complete the room’s mix of color, pattern and texture.

# SelectBlinds and Nautica Bring Coastal Style to the Window

[**Lindsay Brown**](https://www.wf-vision.com/profile/lbrown/)// September 14, 2026

- [![twitter](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/x-logo+black.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=SelectBlinds+and+Nautica+Bring+Coastal+Style+to+the+Window&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fnew-product-annoucements%2Fselectblinds-and-nautica-bring-coastal-style-to-the-window%2F)
- [![facebook](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/facebook.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fnew-product-annoucements%2Fselectblinds-and-nautica-bring-coastal-style-to-the-window%2F)
- [![linkedin](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/linkedin.svg)](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fnew-product-annoucements%2Fselectblinds-and-nautica-bring-coastal-style-to-the-window%2F&title=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fnew-product-annoucements%2Fselectblinds-and-nautica-bring-coastal-style-to-the-window%2F)
- [![pinterest](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/pinterest.svg)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fnew-product-annoucements%2Fselectblinds-and-nautica-bring-coastal-style-to-the-window%2F&media=&description=)
- [![email](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/email.svg)](mailto:?subject=SelectBlinds%20and%20Nautica%20Bring%20Coastal%20Style%20to%20the%20Window&body= "Share by Email")

[Coastal style](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/coastal-style/ "Posts tagged with coastal style") is making its way to the window with a new collaboration between [SelectBlinds](https://www.selectblinds.com/) and [Nautica](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/nautica/ "Posts tagged with Nautica").

The newly launched [Nautica Home](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/nautica-home/ "Posts tagged with Nautica Home") collection translates the lifestyle brand’s classic Americana aesthetic into customizable [window treatments](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/window-treatments/ "Posts tagged with window treatments"), pairing familiar nautical influences with a more relaxed, contemporary approach. Clean stripes, subtle maritime motifs, botanicals, woven textures and easy neutrals give the collection a coastal feel without leaning too heavily into theme.

The assortment spans [roller shades](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/roller-shades/ "Posts tagged with roller shades"), [roman shades](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/roman-shades/ "Posts tagged with Roman shades") and [drapery](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/drapery/ "Posts tagged with drapery"), offering options suited to everything from traditional Cape Cod-inspired interiors to more modern spaces where texture and pattern provide a subtle nod to the coast.

“We’re incredibly excited to partner with Nautica to bring their iconic coastal-inspired style into the home through a new window treatment collection,” said Ashley Damico, VP of Merchandising for [SelectBlinds](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/selectblinds/ "Posts tagged with SelectBlinds"). “Nautica is a brand known for timeless design and effortless lifestyle appeal, and this collaboration allows us to translate that aesthetic into beautifully crafted, customizable blinds and shades.”

For SelectBlinds, the partnership also brings a recognizable lifestyle name into the [custom window coverings](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/custom-window-coverings/ "Posts tagged with custom window coverings") category. Each design is made to measure and available exclusively through the company’s [online platform](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/online-platform/ "Posts tagged with online platform").

The collection extends Nautica’s signature coastal aesthetic into a new category, bringing its mix of classic pattern, texture and relaxed color to window treatments.

[Explore the Nautica Home collection](https://www.selectblinds.com/collections/nautica-home-window-treatments)

# Wilson Fabrics Celebrates 100 Years

[**Lindsay Brown**](https://www.wf-vision.com/profile/lbrown/)// September 14, 2026

- [![twitter](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/x-logo+black.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Wilson+Fabrics+Celebrates+100+Years&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fwilson-fabrics-celebrates-100-years%2F)
- [![facebook](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/facebook.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fwilson-fabrics-celebrates-100-years%2F)
- [![linkedin](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/linkedin.svg)](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fwilson-fabrics-celebrates-100-years%2F&title=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fwilson-fabrics-celebrates-100-years%2F)
- [![pinterest](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/pinterest.svg)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fwilson-fabrics-celebrates-100-years%2F&media=&description=)
- [![email](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/email.svg)](mailto:?subject=Wilson%20Fabrics%20Celebrates%20100%20Years&body= "Share by Email")

[Wilson Fabrics](https://www.wilsonfabrics.com.au/) is celebrating its 100th anniversary in 2026, marking a century of [Australian manufacturing](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/australian-manufacturing/ "Posts tagged with Australian manufacturing"), innovation and growth in the [soft furnishings](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/soft-furnishings/ "Posts tagged with soft furnishings") industry.

Founded by Arthur G. Wilson in 1926, the company began by wholesaling Australian-made and European decorative woven fabrics for drapery and interiors. Today, [Wilson Fabrics](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/wilson-fabrics/ "Posts tagged with Wilson Fabrics") is 100% Australian owned and supplies drapery, blind and sheer fabrics to markets around the world.

Much of that evolution has centered on manufacturing. From its fully vertically integrated mill in [Wangaratta](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/wangaratta/ "Posts tagged with Wangaratta"), Victoria, Wilson Fabrics manages weaving, dyeing, finishing and coating in-house. Over the decades, the company expanded from decorative textiles into coated drapery fabrics, introduced [roller blind fabrics](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/roller-blind-fabrics/ "Posts tagged with roller blind fabrics") in 2000 and continued investing in new weaving and coating technologies.

More recently, Wilson Fabrics has expanded its reach and product offerings, entering the U.S. and European markets in 2015, launching its Australian-made [Whitsundays sheer](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/whitsundays-sheer/ "Posts tagged with Whitsundays sheer") in 2023 and introducing its color-coordinated [COLOUR FLOW](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/colour-flow/ "Posts tagged with COLOUR FLOW") range in 2024.

[![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Wilson-group-300x200.jpg)](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Wilson-group-scaled.jpg) Wilson Fabrics employees, former employees and guests gather at the company’s mill in Wangaratta, Victoria, to celebrate its 100th anniversary.

To commemorate its centennial, the company recently gathered current and former employees and local representatives at its Wangaratta mill to celebrate the people, history and partnerships behind the milestone.

“A 100 year milestone is not achieved alone,” the company shared. “We are incredibly grateful to the generations of employees, our valued customers, suppliers and industry partners who have supported Wilson Fabrics throughout our journey.”

As it enters its second century, Wilson Fabrics says it plans to continue investing in innovation and collaboration while maintaining its Australian manufacturing roots.

![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Tampa-Convention-Center-facade-1.jpg)

# IWCE 2027 Announces Keynote Speaker & Education Lineup

Industry experts will lead sessions across business, design, sales, motorization, installation, marketing, finance and more, March 14-16 at the Tampa Convention Center.

[**Lindsay Brown**](https://www.wf-vision.com/profile/lbrown/)// September 14, 2026

- [![twitter](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/x-logo+black.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=IWCE+2027+Announces+Keynote+Speaker+%26+Education+Lineup&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fiwce-2027-announces-keynote-speaker-education-lineup%2F)
- [![facebook](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/facebook.svg)](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fiwce-2027-announces-keynote-speaker-education-lineup%2F)
- [![linkedin](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/linkedin.svg)](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fiwce-2027-announces-keynote-speaker-education-lineup%2F&title=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fiwce-2027-announces-keynote-speaker-education-lineup%2F)
- [![pinterest](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/pinterest.svg)](https://pinterest.com/pin/create/button/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Findustry-news%2Fiwce-2027-announces-keynote-speaker-education-lineup%2F&media=&description=)
- [![email](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/email.svg)](mailto:?subject=IWCE%202027%20Announces%20Keynote%20Speaker%20&%20Education%20Lineup&body= "Share by Email")

[The International Window Coverings Expo](https://www.iwce-vision.com/) ( [IWCE](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/iwce/ "Posts tagged with IWCE")) has announced its [keynote](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/keynote/ "Posts tagged with keynote") speaker and [education](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/education/ "Posts tagged with education") lineup for IWCE 2027, taking place March 14-16 at the Tampa Convention Center in Tampa, Florida. The 2027 education program brings together experts from across the window covering, design and business communities, with seminars and panel discussions covering finance, sales, leadership, design, color, marketing, [AI](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/ai/ "Posts tagged with AI"), [motorization](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/motorization/ "Posts tagged with motorization"), commercial shading, exterior shading, installation, workroom craftsmanship and more.

![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/tracee.avif) Tracee Murphy, The Design Biz Therapist

Headlining the program is keynote speaker Tracee Murphy, The Design Biz Therapist, presenting “The Human Advantage: Why Understanding People Is Your Greatest Competitive Edge.” Murphy will explore how understanding human behavior and emotional intelligence can help professionals strengthen communication, leadership, teams and customer relationships. Additionally, Murphy will also lead “Conflict Without the Chaos: Turning Difficult Conversations into Stronger Relationships,” focused on navigating challenging conversations while building trust and accountability.

Speaker Lineup:

- Deb Barrett, Window Dressings — Design, trends, sustainability, AI and business
- Kim Boynton, 3/8 and Co., LLC — Exterior shading and outdoor living
- Elle Cole, Elle Cole Interiors — Color and luxury design
- John MacKenzie, Cronopower — Motorization and commercial shading
- Madeleine MacRae — Sales and leadership
- Roger Magalhaes, Shades In Place and Trading Up Consulting — Installation and measuring
- O’D McKewan, Smart Shade Services — Motorization and smart home automation
- Tracee Murphy, The Design Biz Therapist — Business and leadership
- Vince Nigara, Exciting Windows — Business growth and leadership
- Audra Tomme, Creekmore Marketing — Marketing, social media, digital strategy and AI
- Linda Tully, Tully Drapery Shop — Drapery, hardware, design and sales
- Vita Vygovska, Vitalia Inc. — Design and soft treatments
- Michele Williams, Scarlet Thread Consulting — Finance and business strategy


![](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/17/2026/09/Screenshot-2026-09-14-at-1.34.44-PM.png)IWCE 2027 Speaker Lineup

Additional panelists and industry experts will join the program throughout the event. The 2027 seminar lineup is designed to address both the day-to-day needs of window covering professionals and the changes shaping the future of the industry. Attendees can choose from sessions focused on profitability and financial planning, sales, digital marketing and AI, luxury and color, motorization and smart home technology, exterior and commercial shading, measuring and installation, drapery and hardware, and emerging industry trends.

Show leadership shared that education has always been at the heart of IWCE, and that the 2027 program reflects the many different ways our industry is evolving.

> _“We’re bringing together experts who understand the realities of running and growing a profitable window covering business and can give attendees practical ideas, strategies and knowledge they can take home and use.”_

In addition to education, IWCE 2027 will feature two days of exhibits, networking and special events, including the Pirates & Paradise Welcome Party and the 2027 Grace Awards Ceremony. IWCE 2027 takes place March 14-16, 2027, at the Tampa Convention Center, with education beginning Sunday, March 14, followed by the exhibit hall Monday and Tuesday, March 15-16.

**About IWCE**

The [International Window Coverings Expo](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/international-window-coverings-expo/ "Posts tagged with International Window Coverings Expo") (IWCE) is North America’s premier trade show and educational conference dedicated to the window covering industry since 1986. IWCE brings together window treatment professionals, designers, dealers, installers, workrooms, manufacturers, suppliers and industry leaders for education, product discovery, networking and business development.

# Free Webinar to Address Electrical Safety & Compliance in the Window Covering Industry

The “Powering Safety” panel will bring industry experts together to discuss electrical, battery and wireless safety requirements

[**Lindsay Brown**](https://www.wf-vision.com/profile/lbrown/)// September 9, 2026

- [![twitter](https://www.wf-vision.com/wp-content/themes/homefurnishingnews/images/x-logo+black.svg)](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=Free+Webinar+to+Address+Electrical+Safety+%26+Compliance+in+the+Window+Covering+Industry&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.wf-vision.com%2Fwebinars%2Ffree-webinar-to-address-electrical-safety-compliance-in-the-window-covering-industry%2F)

As [motorization](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/motorization/ "Posts tagged with motorization"), [battery](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/battery/ "Posts tagged with battery") power and connected technology continue to expand across the window covering industry, understanding the safety and compliance requirements behind these products is increasingly important for manufacturers, dealers, fabricators and installers.

[Window Fashion VISION](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/window-fashion-vision/ "Posts tagged with Window Fashion VISION") will present “Powering Safety: What You Need to Know About [Electrical Safety](https://www.wf-vision.com/tag/electrical-safety/ "Posts tagged with electrical safety") & Compliance,” a free, 60-minute webinar on Tuesday, October 13 at 1:00 p.m. ET. The live panel discussion will bring together industry experts to explore the electrical, battery and wireless safety standards that apply to today’s window covering products and components, including motors, controls, remotes, batteries, charging systems, sensors and cables.

The discussion will use the industry white paper [_The Importance of Electrical, Battery and Wireless Safety Certifications for the Window Covering Industry_](https://www.wf-vision.com/motorization/the-new-safety-checklist/) as a resource, translating complex requirements into practical information professionals can use when manufacturing, selling, specifying and installing window covering products.

**Attendees will learn:**

- Key electrical, battery and wireless safety requirements
- Risks and potential liabilities associated with uncertified products
- How to identify certified products and components
- Questions to ask suppliers about certification and compliance
- What manufacturers, dealers and installers should know before products reach the customer

**Featured Panelists**

**Tiffany Burlew Regional Product Manager, Appliances, UL Solutions** **Stephen Kuscsik Principal Engineer, UL Solutions** **Daniel Niemirka Window Fashions Global Business Line Product Manager, Somfy Systems, Inc.** **Michael Schratz Chief Product Officer, Rollease Acmeda** **Ralph Vasami Executive Director, Window Covering Manufacturers Association**

Electrical safety considerations extend throughout the product chain, from manufacturing and sourcing to transportation, installation and use. The webinar is designed to give window covering professionals a clearer understanding of their role in navigating compliance and reducing potential risk.

“Powering Safety: What You Need to Know About Electrical Safety & Compliance” is free to attend, but advance registration is required.

# Arvillard (Savoie) : le fabricant d’outillage à main Leborgne (groupe Novalia) nomme comme directeur général Thibaut Natoli

Le nouveau dirigeant succède à Florence Hocq, partie en retraite. Thibaut Natoli, qui a effectué toute sa carrière dans l’industrie, devra notamment de renforcer les synergies entre les trois marques d’outillage du groupe Novalia.

[Mathieu Michel](https://www.lemoniteur.fr/la-redaction/mathieu-michel/)

Publié le 21 septembre 2026 à 18h00

Partager

![Thibaut Natoli, Leborgne](https://www.lemoniteur.fr/resizer/v2/VGMCEQC47ZETLG6D3WZOS7BLJQ.jpg?smart=true&auth=2feb89ca8d121c82a7de5443a8a2da88d534a5627a8a65972370864b4b5895e0&width=732&height=488)

Leborgne

Thibaut Natoli, directeur général de Leborgne.

Thibaut Nato a été nommé par Thibaut et Arnaud Moulin, directeurs du **Groupe Novalia**, à la direction générale de Leborgne, fabricant savoyard, **outillage à main** de jardinage, bâtiment et coupe du bois depuis 1829. Il assure la relève de **Florence Hocq**, désormais retraitée, après 11 ans de direction. Depuis le site d’Arvillard (Savoie), le nouveau directeur général devra renforcer la **complémentarité des trois marques** d’outillage du groupe Novalia : Leborgne, Mob et Mondelin.

Thibaut Natoli a **30 ans d’expérience dans l’industrie** à son actif. Après un diplôme de DUT Génie Mécanique et Productique, puis d’ingénieur en plasturgie, il a exercé dans l’automobile pendant 14 ans, successivement chez Forvia, Harman et Volvo. Il a ensuite été directeur industriel dans le Groupe Piroux (tôlerie mécano-soudure et la peinture industrielle), puis chez MLT Group (jonctions de bande transporteuses), avant de prendre la direction générale de **Bony**(briques réfractaires).

[Mathieu Michel](https://www.lemoniteur.fr/la-redaction/mathieu-michel/), Journaliste à Négoce et au Moniteur des artisans

# Rénovation énergétique : une école modernise son chauffage grâce à une pompe à chaleur hybride en toiture

Installée en toiture, cette PAC hybride monobloc a offert au groupe scolaire une solution efficace de rénovation énergétique : elle a permis de décarboner la production de chaleur tout en conservant les réseaux existants et sans mobiliser de surface au sol.

[Maya Pic](https://www.lemoniteur.fr/la-redaction/maya-pic/)

Publié le 21 septembre 2026 à 17h57

Partager

![Terris Energy](https://www.lemoniteur.fr/resizer/v2/QFV3NCDEMVBINGRHCH35EUNIUI.jpg?smart=true&auth=2bb558c98d109f32f9f9c2d6ea3156e830279cae81eeb2cf58815621a36cc413&width=732&height=488)

Terris Energy

Pompe à chaleur hybride monobloc T Duo 90, de Terris Energy

Comme de nombreux établissements en France, l’école Henri Matisse à Serris (Seine-et-Marne) était chauffée par **un équipement vieillissant alimentant des radiateurs haute température.** Pour sa rénovation énergétique, il s’agissait d’ **optimiser la production de chaleur tout en conservant les émetteurs et le réseau de chauffage existant,** afin de maîtriser les coûts et d’éviter des travaux lourds.

Pour répondre à ces contraintes, la collectivité a retenu la solution de **la pompe à chaleur hybride monobloc T‑Duo 90 (de Terris Energy), de 90 kW,** combinant dans un même bloc une **PAC air/eau** à compresseur inverter et une **chaudière gaz à condensation modulante** (atteignant jusqu’à 85 °C), l’arbitrage entre les deux technologies étant piloté automatiquement par une régulation intégrée.

## **L’hybridation : le bon générateur au bon moment**

L’intérêt de l’hybridation consiste à faire travailler la PAC et la chaudière dans leur meilleure zone de rendement. Ainsi, **la PAC couvre les besoins en mi‑saison et à charge partielle,** quand l’air extérieur est doux et les besoins modérés, et **la chaudière prend le relais lors des pointes de froid hivernales ou des demandes en haute température.** Dans un établissement scolaire l’équilibre est favorable à la part thermodynamique (longues mi-saisons, vacances, pointes courtes). Pour une performance optimisée, la PAC embarque **une régulation native, alternant automatiquement entre 4 modes**(PAC seule, PAC + gaz, gaz seul, dégivrage) et accessible à distance pour le suivi et le diagnostic.

## **Installation simplifiée et mise en service rapide**

Installée directement en toiture‑terrasse du groupe scolaire, la PAC T‑Duo 90 intègre une évacuation des fumées par ventouse et un **circuit frigorifique au R290 scellé et testé en usine,** sans aucune liaison frigorifique ni manipulation de fluide à réaliser sur site. Aucune chaufferie n’est à créer pour l’installation de la PAC. Seul **un local technique accueille le module de découplage hydraulique pré‑monté,** qui sépare le circuit primaire de la sous‑station de distribution. De là partent les départs vers le réseau conservé et les radiateurs existants.

« Cette solution de décarbonation est pragmatique. Dans les écoles, comme dans de nombreux bâtiments publics, les réseaux de chauffage existants ne peuvent pas être entièrement reconstruits. Il faut des technologies capables de s’intégrer simplement, sans travaux lourds, tout en améliorant la performance énergétique. La PAC T‑Duo répond à cette équation, avec une installation en toiture, des radiateurs conservés, les pointes hivernales sécurisées et un fonctionnement optimisé » souligne Antoine Cohignac, directeur général de Terris Energy.

title: Strasbourg : le réseau de chaleur étendu au secteur nord
summary: The Eurometropolis of Strasbourg is expanding its heating network in the northern area with the installation of 33 km of new pipelines by 2030. The first phase consists of 11 km primarily in La Robertsau and is projected to be completed by the end of 2027. This project, funded with an investment of 89 million euros, will provide 110 GWh of heat annually, sufficient for approximately 14,000 homes.

- [Vie du BTP](https://www.lemoniteur.fr/vie-du-btp/)

# Strasbourg : le réseau de chaleur étendu au secteur nord

C. R.

Publié le 21 septembre 2026 à 17h00

Partager

Réservé aux abonnés

Le nouveau réseau de chaleur de l’Eurométropole de Strasbourg déployé dans le nord de l’agglomération est entré en travaux cet été. Ceux-ci prévoient la pose d’une épine dorsale de 33 km de canalisations neuves d’ici 2030. Une première tranche de 11 km jusqu’à fin 2027 se décompose en 11 sections, majoritairement situées dans le quartier de La Robertsau, dans le nord-est de Strasbourg. La société délégataire, Energies décarbonées Eurométropole nord (Eden), associant l’opérateur Réseaux urbains de chaleur Alsace (R-CUA, 65 %) et la Banque des territoires et assistée du BET Lollier Ingénierie, en a réparti les marchés en trois lots : deux attribués à Sogea (groupe Vinci Construction, terrassements) et SGD Réseaux et un à Pontiggia (groupe NGE). La tranche suivante se concentrera surtout dans les villes de Schiltigheim et Bischheim. « Son calendrier et son périmètre exacts restent à préciser », signale François Evrard, directeur général d’Eden. La progression de la pose est liée, en partie, au propre planning de l’Eurométropole pour des rénovations simultanées de réseaux d’eau-assainissement.

## 40 km de conduites cumulées

La programmation se complète de ramifications vers le réseau principal, dès fin 2027 pour les plus précoces, de deux réseaux secondaires dans les communes un peu plus excentrées de Souffelweyersheim et de Mundolsheim, de densifications jusqu’en 2035, de la création d’une sous-station dans la zone du port autonome de Strasbourg et du raccordement au réseau de celui-ci, également piloté par R-CUA. Au total, Eden investit 89 M€ dont 43 % d’aides de l’Ademe et de produits des certificats d’économie d’énergie. Les 40 km de conduites cumulées produiront 110 GWh par an de chaleur, l’équivalent des besoins de 14 000 logements, à 75 % à partir de la récupération de chaleur d’entreprises et de la station d’épuration métropolitaine.

summary: The Fondation François Sommer has inaugurated a new wildlife study center shaped like a hamlet in the Ardennes, comprising nine pavilions within a 1050-hectare site. Designed by architects Frédéric Denisart and Paul Landauer, the pavilions blend harmoniously into the natural landscape with eco-friendly materials.

# Dans les Ardennes, la Fondation François Sommer installe un centre d’études de la faune suavage en forme de hameau de neuf pavillons

C. R.

Publié le 21 septembre 2026 à 17h00

Partager

Réservé aux abonnés

![Ardennes : des pavillons dédiés à l’étude de la faune sauvage](https://www.lemoniteur.fr/resizer/v2/FJWSIB7S3BDQVFTDOIFYLHOEEA.jpg?smart=true&auth=8d297afd33fbca705cd8b1336ccacc59e1ae521e26ece4b118eae38ecbe77f97&width=732&height=488)

CHARLES DURAND

Pour donner une nouvelle ampleur à son site historique de Belval (Ardennes), un domaine de 1050 hectares, la Fondation François Sommer pour la chasse et la nature a choisi d’en étendre son centre dédié simultanément à la formation, la recherche et la création artistique. A cette réalisation inaugurée début juillet, elle a consacré un investissement de 13 M€ TTC, dont 8 M€ HT de travaux). Le duo d’architectes qu’elle a retenu, formé de Frédéric Denisart (Atelier Matières d’Architecture) et Paul Landauer (Atelier Landauer), a traduit l’intention par la conception d’un « hameau » de neuf pavillons (2 500 m2) pour les fonctions - dont celui de la création artistique à l’une des extrémités de la parcelle – ainsi que l’hébergement et la restauration.

« Cette disposition introduit dans le projet la dimension de son intégration paysagère au projet, sur un terrain orienté nord-ouest en légère pente entre forêt et plaine, qui rend aisément visibles les constructions de 15 m de côté, voulues à l’échelle de ce paysage », décrit Frédéric Denisart.

Les toitures donnent à l’ensemble son identité visuelle principale. Elles sont composées de tuiles plates en terre cuite, soit l’une des nombreuses mises en œuvre de matériaux naturels et en circuit courts avec des entreprises locales : structure en ossature bois et charpente lamellé-collé (Le Bâtiment Associé), isolation en paille, parements et maçonneries de pierres pour des murs généreux de 70 cm d’épaisseur, parements intérieurs et parquets en chêne de la forêt de Belval…

title: Dans le Territoire de Belfort, la SEM immobilière Tandem enchaîne les projets de restructuration au service du développement économique local
summary: The SEM immobilière Tandem is set to restructure the Nouvelles Galeries building in Belfort, furthering local economic development. Established in 1988, Tandem has transformed significant industrial sites, managing over 270,000 m² for various industries. With a strong financial track record, the SEM aims to enhance its local contributions through ongoing projects.

# Dans le Territoire de Belfort, la SEM immobilière Tandem enchaîne les projets de restructuration au service du développement économique local

Pour accéder à tous nos contenus, [**abonnez-vous au Moniteur - Edition Abonné**](https://abonnement.lemoniteur.fr/le-moniteur/formule/18/CTA-ST-ART).

Christian Robischon

Publié le 21 septembre 2026 à 17h00

Partager

Réservé aux abonnés

![Belfort : la SEM Tandem s’affirme en pilier de l’économie locale](https://www.lemoniteur.fr/resizer/v2/YWDTLL2TGNEK5HEXPMNBWV37TU.jpg?smart=true&auth=e5af68ca9e4b15b12252d4a95cf39b33e99b1a8b9dea73df1c0eb53963462060&width=732&height=488)

STÉPHANE KURDYBAN - TIME-PROD / TANDEM

Le Techn’Hom s’adapte aux activités de General Electric. Au 1 er plan, un bâtiment tertiaire. A droite, le centre de production et d’essais.

Fortement associée, dans son image et ses actions, à l’édification du quartier industriel Techn’Hom à Belfort, la SEM immobilière locale Tandem ne limite cependant pas son périmètre à celui-ci. Son prochain dossier majeur vient le rappeler. A compter de 2027 et pour une durée de vingt-quatre à trente mois, elle va restructurer le bâtiment des Nouvelles Galeries au centre de la ville, soit 12 092 m2 sur quatre étages acquis pour 6 M€ auprès de son propriétaire privé. Le projet représente un montant de travaux de 14 M€ HT, sous la maîtrise d’œuvre de Sud Architectes. A cette occasion, Tandem agit une nouvelle fois comme le « bras armé » des collectivités locales (la Ville de Belfort, dans le cas présent), qui forment le noyau principal de ses actionnaires : la communauté d’agglomération du Grand Belfort et la mairie, détentrices de 35 % du capital, et la région Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, en charge du développement économique, présente à hauteur de 18 %.

Depuis sa constitution en 1988, Tandem s’est caractérisée par la création et le réaménagement de locaux professionnels, ce qui la rend propriétaire aujourd’hui de 270 000 m2 pour l’industrie, le tertiaire et l’artisanat, occupés par plus de 130 entreprises de tailles très diverses. Le chiffre d’affaires, généré par les études techniques et juridiques, la réalisation et le suivi des travaux ainsi que la gestion locative, se monte à 27,7 M€ en 2025 pour un résul-tat net de 3 M€. « Bénéficiaire à chaque exercice hormis celui de l’année du Covid-19, notre modèle dégage ainsi des dividendes réguliers et permet des incorporations de réserve qui s’ajoutent aux augmentations de capital pour porter celui-ci à 60 M€ : un montant élevé mais nécessaire face à l’ampleur de nos projets », expose le directeur général, Pierre-Etienne Pérol.

## 200 000 m2transformés sur un seul site

En effet, la SEM agit d’abord comme refaçonneuse des vastes sites historiques Bull et Alstom de Belfort. Elle les a réunis pour donner naissance au Techn’Hom, qui forme un ensemble de 110 ha et 200 000 m2 bâtis, dont 35 000 m2 encore disponibles à la location. Elle a consacré à ce parc 200 M€ depuis ses débuts, dont 41 M€ pour adapter 60 000 m2 de General Electric aux évolutions successives des activités sur place du groupe américain. Pour Alstom – qui s’est recentré sur le matériel ferroviaire –, Tandem assure la maîtrise d’ouvrage de la construction, effectuée par le groupement local de PME L’Aube, d’une halle d’essais de 5 700 m2 (10 M€) d’ici début 2027. Elle restructure aussi des surfaces pour de nouvelles activités, comme la fabrication des piles à combustible Inocel depuis l’an dernier sur 11 000 m2. « Nous avons par ailleurs aménagé un axe traversant dans Techn’Hom pour le relier au centre-ville », relève Emilie Tankéré, directrice générale déléguée.

Tandem a en outre piloté la réalisation des deux premiers bâtiments (23 000 m2) de la zone économique de La Jonxion face à la gare TGV Belfort-Montbéliard – en attendant des projets d’extension. Elle fera construire en 2027 la seconde tranche de 1 500 m2 du Village d’artisans de Morvillars, toujours dans l’agglomération belfortaine.

title: Quand l’exécution d’un permis de construire un centre de données dédié à l’intelligence artificielle est suspendue pour absence d’étude d’impact
summary: The Grenoble administrative court suspended a construction permit for an AI data center due to the absence of an environmental impact study. The ruling emphasizes that projects cannot be fragmented to evade environmental evaluation obligations. Inadequate documentation regarding the project's adherence to local regulations also contributed to the suspension.

# Quand l’exécution d’un permis de construire un centre de données dédié à l’intelligence artificielle est suspendue pour absence d’étude d’impact

Avec sa décision du 10 juillet 2026, le tribunal administratif de Grenoble rappelle en creux aux opérateurs qu’un projet ne peut pas être fractionné pour se soustraire aux obligations en matière d’évaluation environnementale.

[Sandrine Pheulpin](https://www.lemoniteur.fr/la-redaction/sandrine-pheulpin/)

Publié le 21 septembre 2026 à 15h57

Partager

Réservé aux abonnés

![Le data center doit sortir de terre à partir de 2029.](https://www.lemoniteur.fr/resizer/v2/ZIBXA3JJFJBKXLLLBHMHEMSKKA.jpeg?smart=true&auth=f71b236ab1337bdcd68f57ded5198c46cf1a543d5276559daf28bd65b6dfa90c&width=732&height=488)

Production Perig Adobe stock

Le juge des référés de Grenoble suspend l'exécution d'un permis de construire un centre de données dédié à l'intelligence artificielle pour absence d'étude d'impact.

L’étude d’impact pour un projet de data center dédié à l’intelligence artificielle n’est pas optionnelle. C’est le sens de la décision du juge des référés du [tribunal administratif de Grenoble du 10 juillet 2026](https://grenoble.tribunal-administratif.fr/decisions-de-justice/dernieres-decisions/suspension-du-projet-de-datacenter-a-alixan "https://grenoble.tribunal-administratif.fr/decisions-de-justice/dernieres-decisions/suspension-du-projet-de-datacenter-a-alixan").

Le maire d’une commune de la Drôme a délivré un permis de construire à une société pour la réalisation d’un « computer center ». **Ces infrastructures, appartenant à la famille des centres de données, disposent d’une puissance de calcul informatique très élevée pour l’hébergement de solutions d’IA.** **Leur fonctionnement nécessite d’importantes capacités d’alimentation électrique, ainsi que des équipements techniques de secours**. L’installation doit en l’espèce s’implanter au sein d’un parc économique, à proximité de la gare TGV de Valence et d’autoroutes. **Plusieurs associations opposées à ce projet ont saisi en référé le tribunal administratif en vue de suspendre l’exécution de l’arrêté autorisant la construction**.

## Urgence et doute sérieux sur la légalité du permis

Parmi les motifs invoqués : l’absence d’étude d’impact environnemental, l’insuffisance du dossier de permis de construire qui ne précise pas que le projet est soumis à évaluation environnementale et la méconnaissance du règlement du plan local d’urbanisme (PLU). Ce dernier proscrit en effet, dans la zone concernée, les installations classées pour la protection de l’environnement (ICPE) soumises à autorisation et les constructions à usage d’industrie sources de risques et de nuisances.

Pour mémoire, deux conditions sont nécessaires pour que le juge fasse droit à une demande de suspension d’une décision : l’urgence et un doute sérieux quant à la légalité de la décision ( [art. L. 521-1 du Code de justice administrative](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000006449326 "https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000006449326")).

S’agissant de la première condition, le juge grenoblois rappelle, conformément à [l’article L. 122-1 du Code de l’environnement](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000051560801 "https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000051560801"), que **les projets doivent être appréhendés dans leur ensemble, « y compris en cas de fractionnement dans le temps** » afin que leurs incidences sur l’environnement soient évaluées dans leur globalité. Aussi, si le projet litigieux prévoit bien « deux phases de travaux », il a été « autorisé dans son intégralité, ce dont témoigne notamment le plan des emprises au sol qui fait apparaître l’installation à l’issue de la seconde phase ».

## Autorisation ICPE et évaluation environnementale

A son terme, poursuit le juge, le centre de données nécessitera une **puissance électrique supérieure à 60 mégawatts (MW)**. Et les groupes électrogènes destinés à assurer son fonctionnement en cas de défaillance de l’alimentation électrique devront disposer d’une puissance thermique nominale encore supérieure.

Or, les **installations de combustion d’une puissance thermique nominale d’au moins 50 MW sont soumises à autorisation au titre de la réglementation ICPE** (rubrique 3110 de la nomenclature). Pour ces installations, une évaluation environnementale – et donc la réalisation d’une étude d’impact - s’impose (cf. [annexe à l’article R. 122-2 du Code de l’environnement](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000054551268 "https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000054551268")).

Aussi, au regard de ces caractéristiques, le projet de « computer center » aurait dû être précédé d’une étude d’impact. En son absence, le permis de construire doit être suspendu conformément à l’ [article L. 122-2 du Code de l’environnement](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000022496595 "https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/codes/article_lc/LEGIARTI000022496595"). Cet article prévoit en effet que **si un recours est fondé sur l’absence d’étude d’impact, le juge des référés doit y faire droit dès que cette absence est constatée**.

Sur la seconde condition, le juge considère qu’un doute sérieux existe quant à la légalité du permis de construire dans la mesure où les ICPE nécessaires au fonctionnement du projet ne peuvent être implantées sur la parcelle d’assiette du projet en raison de son classement par le PLU.

[TA Grenoble, 10 juillet 2026, n° 2605946](https://grenoble.tribunal-administratif.fr/decisions-de-justice/dernieres-decisions/suspension-du-projet-de-datacenter-a-alixan "https://grenoble.tribunal-administratif.fr/decisions-de-justice/dernieres-decisions/suspension-du-projet-de-datacenter-a-alixan")

title: De la rénovation urbaine à la production-rénovation de logements : Anne-Claire Mialot pressentie pour prendre la direction générale de CDC Habitat
summary: Anne-Claire Mialot is being considered for the role of CEO at CDC Habitat, with the decision set for October 2nd. Currently the head of the National Agency for Urban Renovation, she has extensive experience in public service and urban development. If appointed, she will report to the Executive Chairman Clément Lecuivre, filling a position that has been vacant since March.

Décideur

# De la rénovation urbaine à la production-rénovation de logements : Anne-Claire Mialot pressentie pour prendre la direction générale de CDC Habitat

Le conseil de surveillance du bailleur doit se prononcer le 2 octobre sur la nomination ou non de l’actuelle directrice générale de l’Agence nationale pour la rénovation urbaine (Anru).

[Cyril Peter](https://www.lemoniteur.fr/la-redaction/cyril-peter/)

Publié le 21 septembre 2026 à 13h31

Partager

Réservé aux abonnés

![Anne-Claire Mialot, directrice générale de l’Anru](https://www.lemoniteur.fr/resizer/v2/U337W3JLSNOGNOOBOEXTYAAAYI.jpg?smart=true&auth=684416a773d2015ced58bb1f215ecbaa3e61ac90ad85cbe4238d86d0f5be6587&width=732&height=488)

Mathieu Delmestre/Anru

Ancienne conseillère logement d'Emmanuel Macron, Anne-Claire Mialot dirige l’Agence nationale pour la rénovation urbaine (Anru) depuis 2022.

De l’Anru à CDC Habitat. La candidature d’Anne-Claire Mialot, actuelle directrice générale de l’Agence nationale pour la rénovation urbaine, sera étudiée le 2 octobre prochain par le conseil de surveillance de la filiale de la Caisse des dépôts, présidée par l’ancienne ministre socialiste Myriam El Khomri.

En cas d’approbation, **Anne-Claire Mialot « rapportera » au président du directoire Clément Lecuivre** en tant que directrice générale, explique son potentiel nouvel employeur, le 21 septembre. Ce poste est vacant depuis mars dernier : Clément Lecuivre était passé de directeur général à président du directoire, en remplacement d’Anne-Sophie Grave.

## Conseillère logement de Valls, Cazeneuve et Macron

Diplômée de l’Institut d’études politiques de Bordeaux et titulaire d’un DEA d’économie et finances internationales de l’Université Paris Dauphine, Anne-Claire Mialot est **« engagée depuis plus de vingt ans au service de l’action publique** et du développement des territoires », résume CDC Habitat.

Au début de sa carrière, Anne-Claire Mialot exerce plusieurs fonctions de direction au sein de collectivités, notamment la communauté d’agglomération de Cergy-Pontoise (Val d’Oise). Elle travaille par la suite à la Cour des comptes en qualité de rapporteure.

En 2016, elle intègre le cabinet du Premier ministre socialiste Manuel Valls en tant que **conseillère collectivités territoriales, cohésion des territoires et logement**. A son départ pour la primaire du PS dans le cadre de l’élection présidentielle de 2017, Anne-Claire Mialot est restée en place pour conseiller un autre socialiste, Bernard Cazeneuve.

A l’issue de l’élection d’Emmanuel Macron en mai 2017, Anne-Claire Mialot devient sa conseillère sur ces mêmes questions. Elle travaille pour le président de la République jusqu’en décembre 2019 et sa nomination au poste de préfète déléguée à l’égalité des chances auprès du préfet de la Seine-Saint-Denis.

### À lire aussi

- [Pour Patrice Vergriete, président de l’Agence nationale pour la rénovation urbaine, « il faut réussir à dépasser les hostilités au Parlement »](https://www.lemoniteur.fr/mes-magazines/magazine-le-moniteur/pour-patrice-vergriete-president-de-lagence-nationale-pour-la-renovation-urbaine-il-faut-reussir-a-depasser-les-hostilites-au-parlement.ZHYA455BHNN4PAIFTDQBNZU5UY.html)

## CDC Habitat, un producteur et rénovateur de logements

Trois ans plus tard, elle prend la direction de l’Anru, l’établissement public qui pilote les transformations de quartiers entiers. Avec Cédric Van Styvendael, maire socialiste de Villeurbanne (Rhône), et Jean-Martin Delorme, alors président de la section habitat de l’inspection générale de l’environnement et du développement durable (IGEDD), elle co-écrit en 2024 **un rapport qui a nourri les réflexions des gouvernements de François Bayrou puis de Sébastien Lecornu sur le troisième programme de renouvellement urbain**. Celui-ci doit succéder au Nouveau programme national de renouvellement urbain (NPNRU), l’Anru 2 qui approche de la fin.

Formée à l’Institut national des études territoriales (Inet), Anne-Claire Mialot a intégré le corps des administrateurs de l’Etat en 2023, après avoir été titularisée au sein du corps préfectoral en 2021.

**CDC Habitat gère un patrimoine de 573 400 logements**, dont certains sont situés dans un des 447 quartiers à transformer dans le cadre de l’Anru 2 en cours. [En 2025, l’opérateur national a levé le pied sur la rénovation](https://www.lemoniteur.fr/immobilier/en-2025-le-bailleur-social-cdc-habitat-a-leve-le-pied-sur-la-renovation-mais-a-maintenu-une-bonne-cadence-en-termes-de-production.XW2YCFR66ZGBTG77MF3SWHICNQ.html "https://www.lemoniteur.fr/immobilier/en-2025-le-bailleur-social-cdc-habitat-a-leve-le-pied-sur-la-renovation-mais-a-maintenu-une-bonne-cadence-en-termes-de-production.XW2YCFR66ZGBTG77MF3SWHICNQ.html"), mais a maintenu une bonne cadence en termes de production.
